12 — Governed AI Agents: MCP, Hybrid RAG and the AI Gateway

The one idea: in finance an AI agent must never invent a number. It retrieves text with provenance, and it gets every figure by calling a deterministic, typed tool over certified data — then the answer is checked, stamped with the data vintage, and logged. MCP is how the tools are exposed, hybrid RAG is how documents are found, and an AI gateway is where identity, redaction, budgets and routing are enforced.

1. Deterministic-first agents

The model does The tools do
Understand the question, pick tools, plan steps Compute ratios, look up certified metrics, resolve entities
Summarise retrieved text, explain results Compare restatements, run SQL against Gold views
Format the answer, cite sources Return values with vintage tag and source reference

Rule: numbers come from tools, words come from the model. If a tool cannot answer, the agent says so.

2. Model Context Protocol (MCP)

2.1 What it is

MCP is an open protocol for connecting AI applications (hosts/clients) to external capabilities (servers). Messages are JSON-RPC 2.0. Transports: stdio (local process) and Streamable HTTP (remote; it replaced the earlier HTTP+SSE transport and can still stream with SSE).

A server offers three kinds of primitive:

Primitive Controlled by Example
Tools The model decides to call them get_certified_metric(entity_id, metric, period, as_of)
Resources The application attaches them as context doc://annual-report/fy26/page/112
Prompts The user picks them "Credit summary for an issuer" template

2.2 Building a typed MCP server in Python

from datetime import date
from typing import Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
import duckdb

mcp = FastMCP("certified-finance")
con = duckdb.connect("gold.duckdb", read_only=True)

class MetricValue(BaseModel):
    entity_id: str
    metric: str
    fiscal_year: str
    value: float | None
    unit: str
    vintage: str            # Iceberg tag of the certified release used
    source_ref: str         # file hash + page + bbox

@mcp.tool()
def get_certified_metric(entity_id: str,
                         metric: Literal["revenue", "ebitda", "total_debt", "net_worth"],
                         fiscal_year: str,
                         as_of: date | None = None) -> MetricValue:
    """Return a certified metric from Gold. Never estimates: value is null if not certified."""
    row = con.execute("""
        SELECT value, unit, vintage, source_ref FROM gold.metric_as_of(?, ?, ?, ?)
    """, [entity_id, metric, fiscal_year, as_of]).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return MetricValue(entity_id=entity_id, metric=metric, fiscal_year=fiscal_year,
                           value=None, unit="", vintage="", source_ref="not certified")
    return MetricValue(entity_id=entity_id, metric=metric, fiscal_year=fiscal_year,
                       value=row[0], unit=row[1], vintage=row[2], source_ref=row[3])

@mcp.tool()
def resolve_entity(name_or_identifier: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Map a name, LEI, CIN, PAN or ISIN to canonical entity IDs with match confidence."""
    ...

@mcp.tool()
def compare_restatements(entity_id: str, metric: str, fiscal_year: str) -> list[dict]:
    """All bitemporal versions of a fact, with change type, reason and approver."""
    ...

@mcp.resource("doc://{sha256}/page/{page}")
def document_page(sha256: str, page: int) -> str:
    """Text of one page of a landed document, for citation."""
    ...

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()                      # stdio; use transport="streamable-http" to serve over HTTP

Type hints and docstrings become the JSON schema the model sees — be precise; Literal limits the model to valid metrics.

3. Hybrid RAG with provenance

3.1 Why hybrid

Retriever Good at Bad at
BM25 / keyword Exact terms: ISINs, "going concern", "Note 41", rating symbols Synonyms, paraphrase
Dense vectors Meaning: "doubts about survival" ≈ "going concern" Rare identifiers, numbers
Cross-encoder reranker Precisely scoring (query, passage) pairs Too slow to run on the whole corpus

Combine: retrieve top-k from both, fuse, rerank the top ~50, keep the top 5–10.

---
title: Hybrid retrieval pipeline
---
flowchart LR
    Q["Question"] --> F["Metadata filter<br/>(entity, period, vintage, entitlement)"]
    F --> BM["BM25 top 50"]
    F --> DV["Dense top 50"]
    BM --> RRF["Reciprocal rank fusion"]
    DV --> RRF
    RRF --> CE["Cross-encoder rerank"]
    CE --> TOP["Top 8 chunks<br/>with page, bbox, vintage"]
    TOP --> LLM["Model answers<br/>citing chunks"]

Reciprocal rank fusion — simple, robust, needs no score calibration:

def rrf(rankings: list[list[str]], k: int = 60) -> list[str]:
    scores: dict[str, float] = {}
    for ranking in rankings:
        for rank, doc_id in enumerate(ranking, start=1):
            scores[doc_id] = scores.get(doc_id, 0.0) + 1.0 / (k + rank)
    return sorted(scores, key=scores.get, reverse=True)

3.2 Chunk metadata — provenance on every chunk

{
  "chunk_id": "9f2c…:p112:c3",
  "text": "…revenue from operations for the year was ₹ 9,812 crore…",
  "entity_id": "ENT-000431",
  "doc_type": "annual_report",
  "fiscal_year": "FY2025-26",
  "file_sha256": "9f2c…e41a",
  "page_number": 112,
  "bounding_box": [0.08, 0.41, 0.92, 0.47],
  "input_vintage": "vintage_2026_10_31",
  "entitlement": "public"
}

Filter on metadata before similarity search: by entity, period, document type, vintage and, critically, the user's entitlements.

3.3 Qdrant or pgvector

# Qdrant: dense + sparse (BM25-style) vectors in one collection, fused server-side
from qdrant_client import QdrantClient, models
client = QdrantClient("http://localhost:6333")
hits = client.query_points(
    collection_name="filings",
    prefetch=[
        models.Prefetch(query=dense_vec, using="dense", limit=50),
        models.Prefetch(query=models.SparseVector(indices=idx, values=vals), using="sparse", limit=50),
    ],
    query=models.FusionQuery(fusion=models.Fusion.RRF),
    query_filter=models.Filter(must=[
        models.FieldCondition(key="entity_id", match=models.MatchValue(value="ENT-000431")),
        models.FieldCondition(key="entitlement", match=models.MatchAny(any=user_entitlements)),
    ]),
    limit=50,
)

-- pgvector in PostgreSQL
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
CREATE TABLE chunk (chunk_id text PRIMARY KEY, entity_id text, fiscal_year text,
                    body text, tsv tsvector, embedding vector(768), meta jsonb);
CREATE INDEX ON chunk USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
CREATE INDEX ON chunk USING gin (tsv);

-- dense candidates
SELECT chunk_id FROM chunk WHERE entity_id = $1 ORDER BY embedding <=> $2 LIMIT 50;
-- keyword candidates (ts_rank is not exactly BM25, but serves the same role)
SELECT chunk_id FROM chunk WHERE entity_id = $1 AND tsv @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', $3)
ORDER BY ts_rank(tsv, websearch_to_tsquery('english', $3)) DESC LIMIT 50;

Only index Gold / certified documents, and re-index when a new vintage is certified so the answer's vintage matches the data's.

4. The AI gateway

All model traffic passes through one gateway (for example LiteLLM proxy plus your own middleware).

Control What it does
Identity & entitlements Who is calling; which data and models they may use
Redaction Mask PAN, account numbers, names of individuals before text leaves your boundary
Routing Local small models (via Ollama or vLLM) for sensitive or cheap tasks; frontier APIs for hard reasoning
Token budgets & rate limits Per user, team and key; hard stop when exceeded
Kill switch Disable a model, tool or whole agent instantly
Logging & tracing Every request, response, tool call, latency and cost 
# litellm config.yaml (shape)
model_list:
  - model_name: local-small
    litellm_params: { model: ollama/gemma3:12b, api_base: http://localhost:11434 }
  - model_name: frontier
    litellm_params: { model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5, api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }

router_settings:
  fallbacks: [{ "local-small": ["frontier"] }]

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
# Virtual keys per team carry max_budget and rate limits; guardrails hooks run redaction

Applications call the gateway with an OpenAI-compatible API and a virtual key; they never hold provider keys.

5. Tracing and evaluation

5.1 Tracing with MLflow

import mlflow
mlflow.set_experiment("credit-assistant")

@mlflow.trace(name="answer_question")
def answer(question: str, user: str) -> str:
    with mlflow.start_span("retrieve") as s:
        chunks = retrieve(question, user); s.set_outputs({"n": len(chunks)})
    with mlflow.start_span("generate"):
        return generate(question, chunks)

Each trace records inputs, retrieved chunk IDs, tool calls with arguments and results, model, tokens, latency and the final answer — the audit trail for "why did the assistant say this?".

5.2 Evaluation with RAGAS

Metric Question it answers
Faithfulness Is every claim in the answer supported by the retrieved context? (hallucination check)
Answer / response relevancy Does the answer address the question?
Context precision Are the retrieved chunks relevant, and ranked first?
Context recall Did retrieval find everything needed (against a reference answer)?

Build an evaluation set of real questions with reference answers and expected sources. Run it in CI on every prompt, model, chunking or retriever change, and block releases that regress faithfulness.

Add deterministic checks too: every number in the answer must appear in a tool result; every citation must point to a retrieved chunk; vintage must be present.

6. Guardrails checklist for financial agents

  • Tools are read-only by default; any action with side effects needs maker-checker approval (chapter 13).
  • Entitlements are enforced in the tools and retriever, not only in the prompt.
  • Answers carry the data vintage and citations.
  • Personal data is redacted at the gateway; prompts and outputs are logged with retention rules.
  • A kill switch exists per model, tool and agent.

More on LLM engineering basics: LLM engineering and RAG.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why should an agent call get_certified_metric instead of reading the number from a retrieved chunk?
  2. Compute RRF scores (k = 60) for a document ranked 1st by BM25 and 4th by dense search.
  3. Where must entitlement filtering happen in a RAG pipeline, and why is the prompt not enough?
  4. What does faithfulness measure, and what deterministic check complements it?
  5. List four controls an AI gateway enforces.

8. Review checklist

  • All figures come from typed tools over certified data, with vintage.
  • MCP tool schemas use precise types (Literal, dates) and clear docstrings.
  • Hybrid retrieval with metadata and entitlement filters, then reranking.
  • Every chunk carries file hash, page, bbox and vintage.
  • All model traffic goes through the gateway: redaction, budgets, routing, kill switch.
  • Traces stored; RAGAS + deterministic checks gate releases.
